title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 8. Grace to the Avadhuta
html:
The Lord sends His devotees for Nityananda; the meeting in the house of Nandana Acharya; the Lord honours Nityananda; in Srivasa's house He reveals to Him His six-armed, four-armed and two-armed forms

Verse 1

ततः प्रभाते विमले नत्वा तं पुरुषर्षभम्।
गत्वा निजाश्रमं सर्वे स्नात्वा देवार्चनादिकम्॥१॥

tataḥ prabhāte vimale natvā taṁ puruṣarṣabham|
gatvā nijāśramaṁ sarve snātvā devārcanādikam||1||

tatah — then; prabhate — at dawn; vimale — clear; natva — having bowed; tam — to Him; purusha-rishabham — the bull among men; gatva — having gone; nija-ashramam — to their own dwellings; sarve — all; snatva — having bathed; deva-archana-adikam — the worship of the Lord and the rest.

1In the morning, when it grew light, all bowed to the Bull among men and went to their own dwellings; having bathed, worshipped the Lord and performed the other rites,

Verse 2

कृत्वा भुक्त्वा यथान्यायमाजग्मुस्तत्पदाम्बुजम्।
तान्दृष्ट्वा हर्षसम्पूर्णो भगवान्मधुसूदनः॥२॥

kṛtvā bhuktvā yathānyāyamājagmustatpadāmbujam|
tāndṛṣṭvā harṣasampūrṇo bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ||2||

kritva — having performed; bhuktva — having eaten; yatha-nyayam — as was fitting; ajagmuh — came; tat-pada-ambujam — to His lotus feet; tan — them; drishtva — seeing; harsha-sampurnah — full of joy; bhagavan — Bhagavan; madhusudanah — Madhusudana.

2and having eaten as was fitting, they came again to His lotus feet. Seeing them, Bhagavan Madhusudana was filled with joy

Verse 3

ततः प्रोवाच भगवानवधूतः समागतः।
नित्यानन्द इति ख्यातो महात्मा तं समानय॥३॥

tataḥ provāca bhagavānavadhūtaḥ samāgataḥ|
nityānanda iti khyāto mahātmā taṁ samānaya||3||

tatah — then; provacha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; avadhutah — the Avadhuta; samagatah — has arrived; nityanandah — Nityananda; iti — thus; khyatah — called; maha-atma — the great soul; tam — him; samanaya — bring.

3and said: "The Avadhuta1 has come, a great soul named Nityananda. Bring Him here.

Verse 4

हे राम त्वं मुरारे च नारायणमुकुन्दकौ।
गच्छध्वं सत्वरा यूयं यत्रास्ते स महामतिः॥४॥

he rāma tvaṁ murāre ca nārāyaṇamukundakau|
gacchadhvaṁ satvarā yūyaṁ yatrāste sa mahāmatiḥ||4||

he rama — O Rama; tvam — you; murare — O Murari; cha — and; narayana-mukundakau — Narayana and Mukunda; gachchhadhvam — go; satvarah — quickly; yuyam — you; yatra — where; aste — stays; sah — that; maha-matih — great-minded one.

4Rama, and you, Murari, and Narayana and Mukunda2 — go quickly to where that great-minded one is staying."

Verse 5

ततस्तदाज्ञया सर्वे दक्षिणे ग्रामसन्निधौ।
विचार्य तं न दृष्ट्वा ते समीयुस्तत्र सन्निधिम्॥५॥

tatastadājñayā sarve dakṣiṇe grāmasannidhau|
vicārya taṁ na dṛṣṭvā te samīyustatra sannidhim||5||

tatah — then; tat-ajnaya — at His command; sarve — all; dakshine — to the south; grama-sannidhau — near the village; vicharya — having searched; tam — him; na drishtva — not having seen; te — they; samiyuh — came; tatra — there; sannidhim — into (His) presence.

5Then at His command they all went south, to the outskirts of the village; having searched there and not found Him, they returned to the Lord.

Verse 6

ते नत्वा तं सुरश्रेष्ठं प्रोचुर्नास्माभिरद्य सः।
दृष्ट इत्यब्रवीत्तांश्च पुनर्गच्छत साम्प्रतम्॥६॥

te natvā taṁ suraśreṣṭhaṁ procurnāsmābhiradya saḥ|
dṛṣṭa ityabravīttāṁśca punargacchata sāmpratam||6||

te — they; natva — bowing; tam — to Him; sura-shreshtham — the best of gods; prochuh — said; na — not; asmabhih — by us; adya — today; sah — he; drishtah — seen; iti — thus; abravit — He said; tan — to them; cha — and; punah — again; gachchhata — go; sampratam — now.

6Bowing to the Best of gods, they said: "Today we did not see Him." He told them: "Go again, now:

Verse 7

स्वाश्रमे स च द्रष्टव्यः सायाह्ने स महामनाः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा ते यथास्थानं ययुर्हृष्टाः कृताह्निकाः॥७॥

svāśrame sa ca draṣṭavyaḥ sāyāhne sa mahāmanāḥ|
tacchrutvā te yathāsthānaṁ yayurhṛṣṭāḥ kṛtāhnikāḥ||7||

sva-ashrame — in his own lodging; sah — he; cha — and; drashtavyah — is to be seen; sayahne — in the evening; sah — that; maha-manah — great-hearted one; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; te — they; yatha-sthanam — each to his place; yayuh — went; hrishtah — glad; krita-ahnikah — having done their daily rites.

7in the evening that great-hearted one will be seen in His lodging." Hearing this, they went gladly each to his place and performed their daily rites.

Verse 8

ततः सायाह्नवेलायां पथि गच्छञ्जगद्गुरुः।
मुरारिं प्राह दृष्ट्वा तमागच्छ तत्र यत्र सः॥८॥

tataḥ sāyāhnavelāyāṁ pathi gacchañjagadguruḥ|
murāriṁ prāha dṛṣṭvā tamāgaccha tatra yatra saḥ||8||

tatah — then; sayahna-velayam — at evening time; pathi — on the road; gachchhan — going; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; murarim — to Murari; praha — said; drishtva — seeing; tam — him; agachchha — come; tatra — there; yatra — where; sah — he is.

8And in the evening the Teacher of the world, walking along the road, saw Murari and said to him: "Come, let us go to where He is.

Verse 9

समायातो मुनिश्रेष्ठो नन्दनाचार्यवेश्मनि।
तत्राहमपि गच्छामि द्रष्टुं तं पुरुषर्षभम्॥९॥

samāyāto muniśreṣṭho nandanācāryaveśmani|
tatrāhamapi gacchāmi draṣṭuṁ taṁ puruṣarṣabham||9||

samayatah — has come; muni-shreshthah — the best of sages; nandana-acharya-veshmani — to the house of Nandana Acharya; tatra — there; aham — I; api — too; gachchhami — am going; drashtum — to see; tam — that; purusha-rishabham — bull among men.

9The best of sages has come to the house of Nandana Acharya3. I too am going there to see that bull among men."

Verse 10

स मुरारिस्ततो देवो भक्तवर्गसमन्वितः।
प्रेमानन्दरसे मग्नो नन्दनाचार्यसद्गृहे॥१०॥

sa murāristato devo bhaktavargasamanvitaḥ|
premānandarase magno nandanācāryasadgṛhe||10||

sa-murarih — with Murari; tatah — then; devah — the Lord; bhakta-varga-samanvitah — accompanied by the band of devotees; prema-ananda-rase — in the rasa of the bliss of love; magnah — immersed; nandana-acharya-sad-grihe — to the fine house of Nandana Acharya.

10Then the Lord, with Murari and the band of devotees, immersed in the rasa of the bliss of love, went to the fine house of Nandana Acharya

Verse 11

गत्वा ददर्श तं देवं नित्यानन्दं सुखोषितम्॥११॥

gatvā dadarśa taṁ devaṁ nityānandaṁ sukhoṣitam||11||

gatva — having gone; dadarsha — saw; tam — that; devam — divine; nityanandam — Nityananda; sukha-ushitam — comfortably lodged.

11and there saw the divine Nityananda, happily staying in that house.

Verse 12

ततः प्रणम्य तं भक्त्या भगवान्मधुराक्षरम्।
हरिसङ्कीर्तनं कृत्वा ननर्त ललितं मुदा॥१२॥

tataḥ praṇamya taṁ bhaktyā bhagavānmadhurākṣaram|
harisaṅkīrtanaṁ kṛtvā nanarta lalitaṁ mudā||12||

tatah — then; pranamya — bowing; tam — to him; bhaktya — with devotion; bhagavan — Bhagavan; madhura-aksharam — sweet-sounding; hari-sankirtanam — sankirtana of Hari; kritva — performing; nanarta — danced; lalitam — gracefully; muda — with joy.

12Bhagavan bowed to Him with devotion, began a sweet-sounding sankirtana of Hari, and danced joyfully and gracefully.

Verse 13

ततो ननर्त तमनु नित्यानन्दो महायशाः।
हुङ्कारहास्यसम्पूर्णः पुलकाङ्कितविग्रहः॥१३॥

tato nanarta tamanu nityānando mahāyaśāḥ|
huṅkārahāsyasampūrṇaḥ pulakāṅkitavigrahaḥ||13||

tatah — then; nanarta — danced; tam anu — after Him; nityanandah — Nityananda; maha-yashah — the greatly renowned; hunkara-hasya-sampurnah — full of roars and laughter; pulaka-ankita-vigrahah — his body marked with thrilling hair.

13And after Him danced the greatly renowned Nityananda — with roars and laughter, the hair of His body standing on end.

Verse 14

नृत्यावसाने देवस्तु तत्पादरजसा पुनः।
भृत्यस्य मस्तकं पूतमकरोत्कमलापतिः॥१४॥

nṛtyāvasāne devastu tatpādarajasā punaḥ|
bhṛtyasya mastakaṁ pūtamakarotkamalāpatiḥ||14||

nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; devah — the Lord; tu — then; tat-pada-rajasa — with the dust of his feet; punah — again; bhrityasya — of the servant; mastakam — the head; putam — purified; akarot — made; kamala-patih — the Lord of Kamala.

14When the dance was over, the Lord of Kamala purified the head of His servant with the dust of Nityananda's feet.

Verse 15

ततः प्रतस्थे स्वगृहं कथयंस्तत्कथाः शुभाः।
अहो महात्मा कथयत्ययं कृष्णशुभाकरम्॥१५॥

tataḥ pratasthe svagṛhaṁ kathayaṁstatkathāḥ śubhāḥ|
aho mahātmā kathayatyayaṁ kṛṣṇaśubhākaram||15||

tatah — then; pratasthe — set out; sva-griham — for home; kathayan — telling; tat-kathah — talks about him; shubhah — auspicious; aho — ah; maha-atma — the great soul; kathayati — speaks of; ayam — this; krishna-shubha-akaram — Krishna, the source of all good.

15Then He set out for home, telling on the way auspicious things about Him: "Ah, how this great soul speaks of Krishna, the source of all good!

Verse 16

आदौ ज्ञानं भवेत्पुंसस्ततो भक्तिर्हरौ भवेत्।
ततो विरक्तिर्भोगेषु भवेदेव क्रमादिह॥१६॥

ādau jñānaṁ bhavetpuṁsastato bhaktirharau bhavet|
tato viraktirbhogeṣu bhavedeva kramādiha||16||

adau — first; jnanam — knowledge; bhavet — arises; pumsah — in a man; tatah — then; bhaktih — devotion; harau — to Hari; bhavet — arises; tatah — then; viraktih — detachment; bhogeshu — from enjoyments; bhavet eva — surely arises; kramat — in due order; iha — here.

16First knowledge arises in a man, then devotion to Hari, and then, in due order, detachment from enjoyments surely follows."

Verse 17

इत्युक्त्वा पथि देवेशो जगाम निजमन्दिरम्।
कथयामास तत्सर्वं स्वमातुश्चरणान्तिके॥१७॥

ityuktvā pathi deveśo jagāma nijamandiram|
kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṁ svamātuścaraṇāntike||17||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; pathi — on the way; deva-ishah — the Lord of the gods; jagama — went; nija-mandiram — to His own house; kathayam asa — told; tat — that; sarvam — all; sva-matuh — of His mother; charana-antike — at the feet.

17Speaking thus, the Lord of the gods came along the road to His own house and told all this at His mother's feet.

Verse 18

अथापरदिने प्राप्ते नित्यानन्दाय धीमते।
भिक्षां ददौ चन्दनेन कृत्वा सर्वाङ्गलेपनम्॥१८॥

athāparadine prāpte nityānandāya dhīmate|
bhikṣāṁ dadau candanena kṛtvā sarvāṅgalepanam||18||

atha — then; apara-dine prapte — when the next day came; nityanandaya — to Nityananda; dhimate — the wise; bhiksham — alms (a meal); dadau — gave; chandanena — with sandal paste; kritva — having done; sarva-anga-lepanam — the anointing of the whole body.

18When the next day came, He gave the wise Nityananda a meal, having anointed His whole body with sandal paste;

Verse 19

माल्यमर्घ्यं च नैवेद्यं दत्त्वा पूजां चकार च।
एवं सम्पूजितस्तेन नित्यानन्दमहाप्रभुः॥१९॥

mālyamarghyaṁ ca naivedyaṁ dattvā pūjāṁ cakāra ca|
evaṁ sampūjitastena nityānandamahāprabhuḥ||19||

malyam — a garland; arghyam — arghya; cha — and; naivedyam — food offering; dattva — having offered; pujam — worship; chakara — performed; cha — and; evam — thus; sampujitah — honoured; tena — by Him; nityananda-maha-prabhuh — Nityananda Mahaprabhu.

19He offered Him a garland, arghya and food, and worshipped Him. Thus did He honour Nityananda Mahaprabhu.

Verse 20

तत्र स्थित्वा परदिने श्रीवासस्याश्रमं ययौ।
अवधूतं स भिक्षार्थं निमन्त्रणमथाकरोत्॥२०॥

tatra sthitvā paradine śrīvāsasyāśramaṁ yayau|
avadhūtaṁ sa bhikṣārthaṁ nimantraṇamathākarot||20||

tatra — there; sthitva — having stayed; para-dine — on the next day; shrivasasya — of Srivasa; ashramam — to the abode; yayau — went; avadhutam — the Avadhuta; sah — he (Srivasa); bhiksha-artham — for a meal; nimantranam — an invitation; atha — then; akarot — made.

20Having stayed there, on the next day He went to Srivasa's abode, and Srivasa invited the Avadhuta for a meal.

Verse 21

तं पण्डितः प्रणयेन भिक्षां सुसंस्कृतां ददौ।
ततो भुक्त्वा वरान्नं स श्रद्धया पावनं महत्॥२१॥

taṁ paṇḍitaḥ praṇayena bhikṣāṁ susaṁskṛtāṁ dadau|
tato bhuktvā varānnaṁ sa śraddhayā pāvanaṁ mahat||21||

tam — to him; panditah — the Pandita; pranayena — with love; bhiksham — a meal; su-samskritam — finely prepared; dadau — gave; tatah — then; bhuktva — having eaten; vara-annam — the excellent food; sah — he; shraddhaya — with reverence; pavanam — purifying; mahat — great.

21The Pandita lovingly served Him a finely prepared meal, and He partook with reverence of that excellent, great and purifying food.

Verse 22

स्थितस्तत्रैव भगवानागतस्तत्क्षणेन तु।
देवालये शुभे देव उपविश्य वरासने॥२२॥

sthitastatraiva bhagavānāgatastatkṣaṇena tu|
devālaye śubhe deva upaviśya varāsane||22||

sthitah — (as he) stayed; tatra eva — right there; bhagavan — Bhagavan; agatah — came; tat-kshanena — at that moment; tu — indeed; deva-alaye — in the shrine room; shubhe — beautiful; devah — the Lord; upavishya — sitting; vara-asane — on a fine seat.

22And as He stayed there, at that very moment Bhagavan came. Sitting on a fine seat in the beautiful shrine room,

Verse 23

पूर्वलीलामनुस्मृत्य प्रियां मधुरया गिरा।
उवाच पश्य मां त्वं हि मदर्थं कृतवाञ्छ्रमम्॥२३॥

pūrvalīlāmanusmṛtya priyāṁ madhurayā girā|
uvāca paśya māṁ tvaṁ hi madarthaṁ kṛtavāñchramam||23||

purva-lilam — the former pastime; anusmritya — remembering; priyam — dear; madhuraya — with sweet; gira — voice; uvacha — said; pashya — look; mam — at Me; tvam — you; hi — indeed; mat-artham — for My sake; kritavan — have taken; shramam — pains.

23the Lord remembered the dear pastime of old4 and said in a sweet voice: "Look at Me: it is for My sake that You have taken such pains."

Verse 24

अवधूतो मनोवाचं श्रुत्वा तस्य महात्मनः।
अवलोक्य च तं भक्त्या विशेषं नावबुध्यत॥२४॥

avadhūto manovācaṁ śrutvā tasya mahātmanaḥ|
avalokya ca taṁ bhaktyā viśeṣaṁ nāvabudhyata||24||

avadhutah — the Avadhuta; mano-vacham — the heartfelt word; shrutva — hearing; tasya — of that; maha-atmanah — great soul; avalokya — looking; cha — and; tam — at Him; bhaktya — with devotion; vishesham — the special (meaning); na avabudhyata — did not grasp.

24Hearing these heartfelt words of the great soul and looking at Him with devotion, the Avadhuta did not grasp their special meaning.

Verse 25

तज्ज्ञात्वा भगवान्सर्वान्वैष्णवान्प्राह गच्छत।
यूयं गृहाद्बहिः सर्वे ततस्ते निर्ययुर्गृहात्॥२५॥

tajjñātvā bhagavānsarvānvaiṣṇavānprāha gacchata|
yūyaṁ gṛhādbahiḥ sarve tataste niryayurgṛhāt||25||

tat — that; jnatva — knowing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sarvan — to all; vaishnavan — the Vaishnavas; praha — said; gachchhata — go; yuyam — you; grihat — from the house; bahih — outside; sarve — all; tatah — then; te — they; niryayuh — went out; grihat — from the house.

25Knowing this, Bhagavan said to all the Vaishnavas: "Go outside the house, all of you," and they went out.

Verse 26

ततः सन्दर्शयामास नित्यानन्दाय स प्रभुः।
स्ववैभवं स्वमाधुर्यं कौतुकायाखिलेश्वरः॥२६॥

tataḥ sandarśayāmāsa nityānandāya sa prabhuḥ|
svavaibhavaṁ svamādhuryaṁ kautukāyākhileśvaraḥ||26||

tatah — then; sandarshayam asa — revealed; nityanandaya — to Nityananda; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord; sva-vaibhavam — His majesty; sva-madhuryam — His sweetness; kautukaya — playfully; akhila-ishvarah — the Lord of all.

26Then the Lord, the Master of all, playfully revealed to Nityananda His majesty and His sweetness.

Verse 27

स ददर्श ततो रूपं कृष्णस्य षड्भुजं महत्।
क्षणाच्चतुर्भुजं रूपं द्विभुजश्च ततः क्षणात्॥२७॥

sa dadarśa tato rūpaṁ kṛṣṇasya ṣaḍbhujaṁ mahat|
kṣaṇāccaturbhujaṁ rūpaṁ dvibhujaśca tataḥ kṣaṇāt||27||

sah — he; dadarsha — saw; tatah — then; rupam — the form; krishnasya — of Krishna; shad-bhujam — six-armed; mahat — great; kshanat — in a moment; chatur-bhujam — four-armed; rupam — form; dvi-bhujah — two-armed; cha — and; tatah — then; kshanat — in a moment.

27He saw the great six-armed form of Krishna5; in a moment, the four-armed form; and in another moment the Lord became two-armed.

Verse 28

अत्यद्भुतं ततो दृष्ट्वा हर्षेण विस्मयेन च।
जहास च पुनर्धीमान्ननर्त च मुदा सकृत्॥२८॥

atyadbhutaṁ tato dṛṣṭvā harṣeṇa vismayena ca|
jahāsa ca punardhīmānnanarta ca mudā sakṛt||28||

ati-adbhutam — the great wonder; tatah — then; drishtva — seeing; harshena — with joy; vismayena — with amazement; cha — and; jahasa — laughed; cha — and; punah — then; dhiman — the wise; nanarta — danced; cha — and; muda — in joy; sakrit — at once.

28Seeing this greatest of wonders, the wise one, seized with joy and amazement, laughed, and then at once broke into a joyful dance.

Verse 29

देवाज्ञया नाकथयद्रोमाञ्चिततनुर्भृशम्।
वृन्दावनविनोदी तु भ्राता मे त्वं प्रहर्षितः॥२९॥

devājñayā nākathayadromāñcitatanurbhṛśam|
vṛndāvanavinodī tu bhrātā me tvaṁ praharṣitaḥ||29||

deva-ajnaya — by the Lord's command; na akathayat — did not tell; romanchita-tanuh — his body thrilling; bhrisham — intensely; vrindavana-vinodi — who sported in Vrindavana; tu — and; bhrata — brother; me — My; tvam — you are; praharshitah — delighted.

29At the Lord's command He told no one of this, and the hair of His body thrilled intensely. And the Lord, delighted, said: "You are My brother who sported in Vrindavana!"6

Verse 30

इति यः शृणोति नृहरेश्चरितं
सकलं स यज्ञफलमेव लभेत्।
रमते मुकुन्दचरणाम्बुरुहे
हरिनाम तस्य नियतं स्फुरति॥३०॥

iti yaḥ śṛṇoti nṛhareścaritaṁ
sakalaṁ sa yajñaphalameva labhet|
ramate mukundacaraṇāmburuhe
harināma tasya niyataṁ sphurati||30||

iti — thus; yah — who; shrinoti — hears; nrihareh — of Nrihari; charitam — the deeds; sakalam — the entire; sah — he; yajna-phalam — the fruit of sacrifice; eva — surely; labhet — will obtain; ramate — delights; mukunda-charana-amburuhe — in the lotus feet of Mukunda; hari-nama — the name of Hari; tasya — in him; niyatam — constantly; sphurati — shines forth.

30Whoever thus hears all the deeds of Nrihari will surely obtain the fruit of sacrifice; he delights in the lotus feet of Mukunda, and the name of Hari ever shines forth within him.

Thus ends the eighth sarga, "Grace to the Avadhuta" (Avadhuta-anugraha), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. An avadhuta is a wandering renunciate who stands above outward rules; so the poem calls Nityananda.
  2. Rama is apparently Sri Rama Pandita, Srivasa's brother; Narayana is one of the Lord's companions in Navadvipa; Mukunda is Mukunda Datta.
  3. Nandana Acharya is a devotee of Navadvipa in whose house Nityananda stayed.
  4. The pastimes of Krishna and Balarama in Vrindavana; Nityananda is revered as Balarama. Before meeting the Lord He had wandered for many years among the holy places.
  5. The six-armed form (shadbhuja) unites the features of Rama, Krishna and Gaura Himself.
  6. The second line of the verse can also be understood as Nityananda's words to the Lord.
